entries.name: Bjornaer
entries.description: Shapeshifting magi bound to an animal 'heartbeast', more concerned with beasts and the animal side of human nature than with mainstream Hermetic magic; cannot bond with familiars, and are organized into six clans split between Harmonist and Wilderist philosophies. A Mystery Cult -- joining teaches the Outer Mystery of taking the heartbeast's form.
entries.benefit: Heartbeast, beginning score of 1 in the Heartbeast Ability.

entries.name: Bonisagus
entries.description: A true lineage descended from Bonisagus, who invented the Hermetic theory of magic (his student Trianoma masterminded the Order's formation); split between Theoretical magi who push the boundaries of Hermetic magic and Political 'magi Trianomae' who work to keep the Order together.
entries.benefit: Puissant Magic Theory (researchers) or Puissant Intrigue (politicians).

entries.name: Criamon
entries.description: A secretive, enigmatic House whose members mark their bodies with arcane symbols and pursue the mystical 'Enigma', showing little interest in Order politics. A Mystery Cult built around this philosophy.
entries.benefit: The Enigma, beginning score of 1 in Enigmatic Wisdom.

entries.name: Ex Miscellanea
entries.description: A large, loosely organized House of magi from many non-Hermetic magical traditions, admitted as a group after its founder Pralix's rival Ordo Miscellanea was absorbed into the Order; the easiest House to join from outside.
entries.benefit: A free Minor Hermetic Virtue, a free Major non-Hermetic Virtue and a compulsory Major Hermetic Flaw, for the tradition within the House; all in addition to the normal allowance.

entries.name: Flambeau
entries.description: Aggressive, martial magi specializing in fire (or destructive Perdo) magic, valued for their fearlessness in the Order's defense but prone to causing trouble; carries a strong tradition of honor and chivalry.

entries.name: Guernicus
entries.description: A true lineage descended from Guernicus, providing the Order's judges (Quaesitores) who investigate crimes and enforce the Code of Hermes; divided between Traditionalists and Transitionalists over how strictly the Code should be applied.

entries.name: Jerbiton
entries.description: Magi drawn to art, culture, and the mundane world, often from noble or artisan backgrounds, working to keep the Order on good terms with Church and nobility; loosely organized into interest-based leagues rather than a single structure.
entries.benefit: A Minor Virtue relating to scholarship, arts or mundane interaction.

entries.name: Mercere
entries.description: A true lineage descended from the now-unGifted Founder, providing the Order's messengers -- the Redcaps -- regardless of whether individual members have The Gift; all Mercere, Gifted or not, are recognized as full magi.
entries.benefit: Puissant Creo or Puissant Muto. (An unGifted Redcap is a companion with the Redcap Virtue instead.)

entries.name: Merinita
entries.description: Magi devoted to the study and defense of faerie, often as strange as the creatures they study, largely isolated from the rest of the Order. A Mystery Cult whose members are Initiated into Faerie Magic.
entries.benefit: Faerie Magic, beginning score of 1 in the Faerie Magic Ability. A magus without a faerie-related Virtue or Flaw has a Warping Point.

entries.name: Tremere
entries.description: A tightly disciplined true lineage valuing hierarchy, strategy, and respect for superiors; apprentices' voting sigils are held by their parens until won in Certamen, concentrating the House's political power in few hands.

entries.name: Tytalus
entries.description: Magi who thrive on conflict and constant challenge, believing struggle against ever-stronger opposition is the path to mastery; still distrusted since its 10th-century leaders were executed for diabolism, and currently split between two rival claimants to Primus.

entries.name: Verditius
entries.description: Master craftsmen with unsurpassed skill at enchanting items, though almost all share their Founder's Flaw of needing casting tools to cast Formulaic spells. A Mystery Cult riddled with long-running personal vendettas between its members.
